canonical_name: Neron-Tate canonical height on an elliptic curve
canonical_human_claim: For an elliptic curve E over a number field K, the normalized limiting height hat_h(P) = (1/2) lim_{n to infinity} 4^(-n) h_x([2^n]P) exists for every P in E(K), differs from (1/2)h_x(P) by a bounded amount, is quadratic, is nonnegative, and vanishes exactly at torsion points.
domain_and_universes: K is a number field; E is an elliptic curve over K; P,Q range over E(K); m ranges over Int; the proposition is intended for Lean universe levels forced by the selected mathlib model.
hypotheses: K is a finite extension of Rat
E is a nonsingular elliptic curve over K
h_x is the selected absolute logarithmic projective x-coordinate height
conclusions: the defining canonical-height limit exists for every P
hat_h(P) - (1/2) h_x(P) is uniformly bounded in P
hat_h(P) = 0 if and only if P is torsion
degenerate_and_boundary_cases: the identity point requires an explicit x-height convention
torsion points are included and form precisely the zero-height kernel
the number-field hypothesis may not be weakened to an arbitrary field
